cases.reason: Format 2 (key-level) printed identically, ellipsis on the brace group in both.

OBJECT-COMPUTER general format is printed the same in both (CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION and PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, both IS and FOR forms). 'Defines a national collating sequence' rests on 2002 Table 7 and ALPHABET GR7 a)-k), which match 2023 Table 6 row for row (UTF-8 and UTF-16 have no collating sequence in both). No data-name operand, no CD reach, no 2002-only alphabet operand.

LOCALE ... IS literal-4 and ORDER TABLE ... IS literal-9 carry the same ordinals in both formats. The literal kinds are the same set. 2002 8.8.3.3 GR3 and 2023 8.8.3.3 GR3 both let a concatenation expression stand for a literal, so that adds nothing on the 2002 side. Zero-length literals are a 2023-only widening, banned by a separate 2023 rule.
alphabet-name-clause is printed the same in both editions (same alphanumeric and national branch operands). The implied ALPHANUMERIC phrase feeds the same downstream rules (SR14b, Table 7/6, GR7a).

locale-name-2 in the ALPHABET clause's LOCALE [locale-name-2] alternative, in both branches, in both editions. The OBJECT-COMPUTER locale-phrase-2 operand of the same name is governed by that paragraph's own SR3, the same in both. Only the rule number moved.

The rule asks only for the implementor's list of switch-, feature- and device-names. In 2002, SR6 also lets a feature-name mnemonic be used in SEND, but which statements may use a name is SR6/SR7's concern. The list itself (C01, CSP; DOC-A.1-190) is one list at every edition, so the 2023 evidence holds. No 2002-only name kind.
The 2002 user-defined function-specifier (Format 1, AS literal-3) is the 2023 user-defined-function-specifier (AS literal-5). The rule names neither literal. The self-reference case is the same.
program-specifier is the same apart from the AS literal's ordinal, which the rule does not name. Containing program definitions mean the same in both.
Without EXPANDS, interface-specifier is INTERFACE interface-name-2 [AS literal-2] in both. class-name-4 vs object-class-name-4 is inside EXPANDS only. The external repository requirement is the same.

In 2002, data-name-n in a general format includes subscription if needed (5.1.3), and 2014 Annex E.2 item 25 confirms that in 2002 it 'may be subscripted' unless a rule says otherwise. The 2002 RECORD KEY clause's own SR1 says only 'may be qualified'. So RECORD KEY IS K(1), for K a PIC X item under OCCURS in the FD record, is legal 2002, and SR2 governs it: an alphanumeric element is accepted, a numeric one is refused. 2023 SR1 removes every key subject to an OCCURS, so the 2023 verdict covers no subscripted key. Probe rk_sub.cob (alphanumeric element): refused at --std 2002 with COBOL2024, which cites §2023 clauses. That is WRONG against the 2002 text, a compiler defect (it rejects legal 2002 source). rk_sub_num.cob is refused too, but by COBOL2024 instead of SR2.

In 2002, SOURCE IS { data-name-2 } ... may name subscripted table elements (5.1.3; 2014 E.2 item 25), and SR5 gives record-key-name-1 the class and category of those elements. 2023 SR1 forbids any OCCURS, so the 2023 verdict says nothing about a key built from subscripted SOURCE parts. The compiler refuses every subscripted key operand at --std 2002 (COBOL2024; probe rk_sub.cob shows the mechanism), so this 2002 case is also a compiler defect.

cases.reason: Same cause as SR6. In 2002, data-name-1 in the key-level format may be subscripted. So 'specified in more than one COLLATING SEQUENCE clause' must be decided for a subscripted key, for example OF AK(1) in one clause and OF AK(1) again in another. That 2002-only case is removed in 2023 by the new SR6 ban on subscripting. The compiler refuses any subscripted key-level operand at --std 2002 (cs_sub.cob, COBOL2024), so this 2002 scope has no evidence and the refusal is a compiler defect.

compiler-defects-found.summary: At --std 2002, COBOL2024 refuses a subscripted RECORD KEY, ALTERNATE RECORD KEY, RELATIVE KEY and key-level COLLATING SEQUENCE OF operand. It cites §2023:8.4.2.2.2 and the 2023 'shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses' rules. 2002 has neither: its key clauses' SR1 says only 'may be qualified', and §2002:5.1.3 together with §2014:E.2 (item 25) make data-name-n subscriptable unless a rule forbids it.
